We are team developers s'29 (Assiut Event) for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge.

Skills: We excel in Web Development and Documentation, and already deployed a live web prototype tracking NASA's discarded equipment.

Why Join: We have a working project, an organized workflow, and are ready to win.

Looking For: UI/UX Designers, Front-End Developers, and Storytellers for animations and narratives.
summary:
We developed "Abandoned But Not Forgotten | Little Space Explorers," an interactive educational web platform designed to bring the stories of retired and distant NASA spacecraft to life for young learners and curious minds. Using official archives from NASA JPL, Solar System Exploration, and the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, our platform lets users explore historic missions across the Moon (Apollo 11), Mars (Opportunity and Ingenuity), and Deep Space (Voyager 1, complete with a live distance tracker).
This project addresses the challenge of making complex space history and scientific data engaging and accessible to children. Through an interactive Space Map, a hands-on Space Lab, collectible Explorer Badges, and a "Read to me" audio feature, users actively discover where these machines landed and what they achieved. Preserving these legacies is vital to inspiring the next generation of space explorers and honoring humanity's pioneering robotic ambassadors.
details:
What Our Project Does & How It Works
"Abandoned But Not Forgotten | Little Space Explorers" is an interactive, 3D educational web platform that brings the stories of NASA’s retired and distant spacecraft to life for children, students, teachers, and space enthusiasts. Instead of reading dense technical archives, users become "Junior Space Explorers" and navigate three main interactive sections:

  • 3D Space Map: Users can rotate, zoom in, and click on 3D models of the Moon, Mars, and Saturn (Deep Space) to inspect interactive pins for iconic missions like Apollo 11 Eagle Lander, Apollo 15 Lunar Rover, Opportunity Rover (Oppy), Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, Cassini Saturn Orbiter, and Voyager 1 (complete with a live distance tracker from Earth).
  • Interactive Hangar (Machines): Users tap animated cards of famous NASA space heroes to zoom in and uncover their secret mission files and scientific achievements.
  • Space Lab & Activities: An interactive learning hub featuring a planetary "Weight Calculator" (comparing the user's weight and jump height on the Moon or other destinations against space buddies like Ingenuity), a "Find the Space Treasures" scavenger hunt across the 3D map, and a custom "Junior Space Explorer" certificate generator.

Benefits, Creativity & Intended Impact
Information about past space missions is often scattered across complex websites that can feel overwhelming or boring to young learners. Our platform creatively combines storytelling, gamification (collectible Explorer Badges and Souvenir Vault), 3D visualization, and accessibility features (such as the "Read to me" audio narration and simple, child-friendly language) into one cohesive experience. Our intended impact is to spark curiosity in STEM, honor the engineering legacy of humanity's robotic pioneers, and inspire the next generation of space explorers.

Tools, Technologies & Design Considerations
We built the platform using modern web development technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and interactive 3D rendering) and deployed it on Vercel for fast, free, and reliable global access across desktops, tablets, and mobile devices without requiring any downloads or logins. All scientific facts and mission histories are grounded in official archives from NASA JPL, NASA Solar System Exploration, and the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal.
